findings.reason: a section that repairs this exact defect for one index and explicitly rejects over-fetching ("it reproduces the defect at the next size") must state the sibling index's fate — extend the filter-property mechanism to it or show it does not starve — or the plan ships the code fix while the equally-named signal goal is left on the rejected pattern.
findings.text: §12 fixes the facility post-filter starvation for `CodeChunk` and says in its own text only that "the signal and wiki-chunk embeddings are left alone", without stating why the same owner cannot carry them, while `_vector_search_signals` post-filters `s.facility_id = $facility` after the ANN cut (`where_clauses=where_parts`, over-fetch `max(k*2,50)`) and §1 names `search_signals` answering for jt-60sa as a plan goal

findings.reason: a done-when whose check cannot return the named result must be narrowed (e.g. `--glob '*.py'`) before the node is dispatched, or the worker cannot reach the declared measure.
findings.text: the named check `rg 'CREATE VECTOR INDEX' imas_codex` matches only `ensure_vector_indexes` cannot pass as written: the literal also appears in the prose of `imas_codex/graph/AGENTS.md:354` ("never hand-write `CREATE VECTOR INDEX`"), which survives any Java/Kotlin-free source dedup, so the section's own verification of the de-duplication is unsatisfiable

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §12 adds filter metadata to the existing schema→generated-map→`ensure_vector_indexes` owner chain and a pre-filter form on the existing builder rather than a new module, and §9 collapses three inline `DataAccess` write sites into one `persist_data_access`; neither adds a shallow wrapper layer.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §12 applies the in-index filter mechanism to `CodeChunk.embedding` only and leaves `_vector_search_signals` (search_tools.py:454) and the document/wiki vector searches on the same facility post-filter, with no stated reason the owner cannot be extended to them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §12 states the one schema annotation it adds and the `where_clauses` post-filter it retires, §15 deletes five DDL copies, §9 and §11 add no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family, and §2's typed slots account for the keyword field they replace.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every implementable section cites and extends an existing owner rather than proposing a parallel one: §12 extends `build_vector_search` / `ensure_vector_indexes` / `GraphSchema.vector_indexes` through the schema→generator→client chain, §14 uses the existing `discover paths --root` scope and `discover code --path-prefix`, §11 moves the existing `NEO4J_URI` check inside `resolve_neo4j` (its single owner), §9 targets the existing `probe_remote_environment` callers, and §15 names the five hand-written DDL copies it deletes.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no section adds a thin layer over existing machinery; §15 removes five hand-written copies in favour of the owner's `ensure_vector_indexes`, and §9 makes `get_python_status` consume a resolved environment instead of re-probing the same facility.
